title: Number Patterns: Linear Sequences and the General Term
seo_title: Grade 10 Number Patterns Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Investigate number patterns leading to those where there is a constant difference between consecutive terms, and the general term is therefore linear.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 10 number patterns worksheets: linear sequences, the general term, finding terms and positions. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: n must be a natural number.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A linear sequence has a constant first difference d.
  • General term: Tₙ = dn + c, or Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d.
  • To find a term, substitute n. To find a position, solve Tₙ = value for n.
  • n must be a natural number.

Examples

Example

4; 11; 18; 25; …

d = 7

Tₙ = 7n − 3

Answer: T₄₀ = 277

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
One difference onlyCheck all the differences.
n or Tₙ?n is the position; Tₙ the value.
The constant7n − 3, not 7n.

items.q: What is the next term? 2, 4, 8, 16, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 2 each time. 16 × 2 = 32.

items.q: What is the next term? −7, −12, −17, −22, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: subtract 5 each time. −22 − 5 = −27.

items.e: The difference is always 8, so it is arithmetic.

c: Yes, because it is bigger than 5
No, because n would not be a whole number
items.e: 5n + 9 = 63 gives n = 54 ÷ 5, which is not a whole number. So no.
